steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat until hot. Add corn kernels until 2 to 3 pop; stir in white and brown sugars. Cover pot with a lid; agitate pot in a circular motion on the stove. Allow corn to pop, agitating pot constantly, until popping rate slows down to 1 pop every 2 to 3 seconds. Remove pot from the stove; shake pot until popping stops. Transfer popcorn to a large bowl; cool to room temperature. Break apart large popcorn clumps by hand; season with salt.

raw_recipe.headline: State Fair Kettle Corn
raw_recipe.description: This state fair kettle corn recipe uses just a few ingredients — oil, popcorn kernels, white sugar, brown sugar, and salt. It will be an instant hit.
raw_recipe.name: State Fair Kettle Corn

review.reviewBody: I love the taste of this kettle corn, but for future makers you need to be careful. I ran into a problem with the sugar, following the directions I waited for a few pieces to pop before adding it in and got splattered by oil, was actually stirring the sugar so it would melt enough that I could shake the pot and the sugar would be a sticky sugary paste the kernels just stuck to; again I ran into the problem of the oil splattering. To say the least my first batch burned on the bottom. The second time I made it, I added the sugar and the kernels in at the same time and the popcorn turned out delicious.

I became an adult when I realized I could buy all the Cracker Jack I wanted and didn't need to ask anyone's permission. I've always wanted to make my own but am too lazy to go through the process of making caramel corn. This recipe is not quite Cracker Jack in the absence of molasses. However, I am pleasantly surprised at how tasty it turned out and it's a good and, most importantly, quick and easy substitute. Some tips: 1. Get a Whirley Pop, preferably the original genuine model and not one of the many knock-offs. Greatest invention since the wheel. You'll get much more consistent results with less burning and also greatly reduce the risk of being splattered by hot oil, noted by other reviewers. 2. Use avocado oil instead of corn oil. Avocado oil has a higher smoke point, especially preferable because of the temperatures needed when you... 3. Use mushroom popcorn, not generic supermarket kernels. Mushroom is generally a better choice for coated popcorn recipes as the kernels pop up as big puffy balls (somewhat like those in Cracker Jack) instead of the florets of regular popcorn varieties. (Expect more hulls, though.) The best, most consistently fresh and reliable mushroom popcorn I've found comes from nuts dot com. Avoid the Amish Country and similar brands sold via Amazon; sitting in a warehouse does not enhance their performance in a popper. Mushroom popcorn comes out best when popped at very high temperatures. I turn my burner all the way up to the max and crank the Whirley Pop like a demon. 4. I used 1/2 tsp salt with the above 1X recipe quantities. 5. I used Imperial Sugar (brand) Dark Brown Sugar -- because I like the taste of molasses. This particular brand is very dark, almost bitter and definitely not to everyone's tastes. Delicious! Now if I could figure out how to add more molasses into the mix without risking burning...

I made this in the microwave. Delicious! I did make a few adjustments. I only used1/8 cup of oil and I added 1/2 t of vanilla. I made it in my microwave popcorn bowl with lid. I used the popcorn setting on the microwave. It is a great snack!

I have made this a couple of times. The first time I added the sugar and popcorn at the same time and it burned. I discovered that if you make the sugar mixture separate from the popcorn it doesn't burn. I use 3 Tablespoons of margarine, 3 Tablespoons Brown sugar and 3 Tablespoons white sugar and 1 teaspoons of cinnamon

Excellent recipe! I adapted it to my electric popcorn popper and it was GREAT! (1/4 C oil to 1/2C popcorn - let them heat until they are "sizzling" then sprinkle sugars over. I shook the popper to make sure nothing stuck or burned.)YUMMY!

Exceptionally GOOD! I do think it is more like caramel corn than kettle corn however. I used 2 Tbs. of both the white & brown sugars & 1/3 cup of popcorn in 1/4 cup of veg. oil. I used medium heat. I think the key is to keep that pot a shakin' pretty much throughout the cooking process. The brown sugar makes it thick & the kernels seemed slow to pop, but patience paid off. This was one of the best snacks I've had in a very, very long time! I'll be making this often!!

The sugar scorched before half the popcorn had popped. I plan on doing this again, but popping the corn first, separately, and then tossing the sugar and butter (substituting for the oil) in a bowl to control the distribution.

this was a great recipe! It's more like a cross between Kettle and Caramel corn. if you follow the recipe exactly you should have no trouble (after burning my first two batches I know!). One helpful thing I learned make sure you use a much larger pot than you think you need (ie a dutch oven etc.) and be sure the popcorn covers the bottom of the pan completely, that way when you add the sugars it sits on the corn, not the pan.

Awesome! I doubled all ingredients, except the oil I left 1/4 cup. I also threw in the salt (maybe 1/2 teaspoon) along with the sugars. It tasted like a light version of caramel popcorn but was ready in 5 minutes! I know by the way the kids inhaled it, I will be making it a lot! Thanks happy cook!

The oil-to-corn ratio seems way off (I used half as much oil as corn), and I added the seasonings after the corn was pretty much done popping because I was afraid of getting a melted, burned mess. I also added half a teaspoon of cinnamon, which made it awesome.
I used 1/2 cup corn kernels with 3T popping oil. I did 4T white sugar and 4t brown. This gets really hot. Be ready with oven mits. I had to stir to get it going and keep it from sticking

This was a semi success. At least the sugar didn't burn in the pan like the last recipe I tried. It's not without fails though as the moment I added the sugar, the temp dropped and it took quite a while to get back to popping again, and the sugar tended to just sit on the bottom in one spot and not move even though vigorous swirling motion as directed was used. I ended up having to remove the lid and use a utensil to try to move the sugar clump around quickly. The sugar eventually melted and carmelized, but you have to be quick in getting it out of the pan as the heat from the pan started to burn it as soon as all the popcorn was dumped out. I'm just going back to the old tried and true oven method as it works every single time. This was disappointing too. It sort of worked, but not really.
I used 4 Tablespoons coconut oil, 1/4 cup honey...YUM

Perfect first and second time! An easy quick recipe better than any other, well maybe one exceptIon would be a State Fair! 
It’s an easy simple recipe as easy as microwave popcorn, no big deal to wash a heavy non-stick Dutch oven. It’s so worth the little extra effort! Another thing I like is the ease in changing the amount of servings. Movies and popcorn perfect for 2020 Covid19 sheltering in place. Good old fashioned popcorn brings back memories for me, for others perhaps creating new memories

This popcorn needs to be moved around frequently. The brown sugar didn't melt completely and caused some burning and smoke from the electric burners on the stove. Overall the popcorn turned out descent.

Absolutely terrible, what a waste of ingredients and time. I wish I read the reviews prior, with tips on the oil temp and when to add the sugar.

I have a giant, burnt clump of popcorn in the garbage and spent 15 minutes cleaning the burnt mess from my pot.

My advice: read the other reviews and pay attention to the tips, otherwise this will be total garbage.
Bland.

Made this recipe but I need to warn everyone, when oil gets hot it splatters, so if you reach over or into the hot pan, it can splatter on you!!!! 

Anyhoo, I doubled the popcorn and the sugar but not the oil, oh and used coconut oil instead of canola oil and it turned out PERFECT!!! It was a BIG HIT!!! Hubs and kids devoured the whole batch while it was still on the stove!!!!!!!!
I too used 1/4 cup oil an a 1/2 corn. Needed more firm to the ratio. I'll only use white sugar next time for that true Texas State Fair kettle corn taste. Robin - Beach City Texas

I used a whirly pop popper and increased the amounts 2x. Delicious! My wife isn't much of a popcorn eater, but she loves kettle corn. I make this without her knowing it...the look on her face when she ate some was priceless..she asked for a dish full!
